args.message:
Fix FIN-212: use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money

The docstring already specified ROUND_HALF_EVEN but the implementation
used ROUND_HALF_UP, breaking tests/test_money.py (e.g. 2.665 rounded to
2.67 instead of 2.66).

args.head: fix/fin-212-round-half-even
args.title: Fix FIN-212: use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money
args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build failure in `tests/test_money.py` was caused by `src/money.py` implementing `ROUND_HALF_UP` despite its docstring (and FIN-212) specifying banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`).

## Change
- Replaced `ROUND_HALF_UP` with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `round_money`.

## Verification
- CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986` **passed**, including `test_money.py` (2.675 → 2.68, 2.665 → 2.66).

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

- **Diagnosed**: `src/money.py` claimed banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, per FIN-212) in its docstring but actually used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, which is why `tests/test_money.py` failed (2.665 must round to 2.66, not 2.67).
- **Fixed** on a new branch `fix/fin-212-round-half-even` with a commit switching the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.
- **Ran CI** on the branch (run `ci-0001`, commit `08d3cd5986`) — it **passed**.
- **Opened PR #101** against `main` requesting review from **alex**: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101
  - Note: the standard PR API returned 503, so I opened it via the legacy API (same effect, with an idempotency key to avoid duplicates).

Merging will require code-owner approval per org policy, so I left the PR open for review.
